comments.story_title: Some Days I Can’t Do Life – When everyday life becomes a struggle (2020)
comments.text_zh: 除了吃药，我什么都试过了。我害怕自己不再“是我自己”——或者别人就是这么跟我说的——又或者吃药会让这个问题变得更真实。总之，我最后还是吃了药，而我从来没有像现在这样觉得自己就是自己，或者说是我想成为的那个人。我能工作、学习、社交，住在一个（相对）干净的公寓里，还会出门走走。我花了太久才接受：抑郁症不全是我的错，它是一种疾病，我需要去看真正的医生。对那些正在受苦的人，或者认识正在受苦的人的人（这大概就是所有人），我真的很推荐这个讲座：[视频] 它超级有意思，把抑郁症的各种成因串了起来——童年创伤、日常经历，一直讲到神经元和化学反应。它真的很有助于把这件事外在化。
comments.text: I tried everything except for medication. I was afraid i would no longer be 'myself' or that's what other people told me — or maybe that it would make the problem more real. Anyway, I eventually took meds, and I have never felt more myself, or the person I want to be. I work, learn, socialize, live in a (relatively) clean apartment, which I leave to go outside. It took me way too long accept that depression is not all my fault, that it's a disease, and that I needed to see a real doctor. For those who suffer, or know those who suffer (that's probably everyone) I really recommend this lecture: [VIDEO] It's super interesting, it ties all the causes of depression together — childhood trauma, everyday experience, down to the neuron, and chemical reactions. It really helps externalize it.

comments.text_zh: Robert Sapolsky 对抑郁症作为一种习得性无助有非常精彩的论述。我们在受虐待的动物身上能看到这一点：[视频] 在某种程度上，你和任何其他动物并没有太大区别。经过足够多的条件作用，你会相信自己对自己的人生毫无掌控力，于是你就坐在那里承受电击，盼着它快点结束。或者更糟，你会失去判断力，以为解决你当前（很可能是暂时的）处境的唯一办法就是（肯定是永久地）结束自己的生命。
comments.text: Robert Sapolsky has a fantastic discussion of depression as a form of learned helplessness. We see it in abused animals: [VIDEO] You are not much different from any other animal at some level. With enough conditioning you will believe that you have no agency over your own life, and you’ll just sit there and take the shocks hoping it ends soon. Or worse, you’ll lose perspective and imagine the only solution to your current (likely temporary) circumstance is to (definitely very permanently) end your own life.

comments.why_zh: 关于抑郁症作为一种疾病的相关讲座。
comments.quote_zh: 一位非常杰出的神经科学家关于此话题的高度相关讲座
comments.text_zh: 过去我在 HN 上一直非常直白地表达自己对抑郁症的立场，尤其是：说“man up（硬气点）”这种话是荒谬的。抑郁症和地球上其他所有疾病一样，不是靠“man up”就能扛过去的东西。它是一种恰好表现在人格所在那些地方的疾病。在一个随意、不知情的外人看来，抑郁症像是一种行为选择。但它不是。你不会因为软弱就得抑郁症，就像你不会因为软弱就得癌症一样。抑郁症每年致死的人数也比癌症多。癌症大约 2 万——抑郁症大约 3 万。（一位非常杰出的神经科学家关于此话题的高度相关讲座：[VIDEO]）——话虽如此，Ed Weissman 说了一句不恰当的话。这里的每一个人，包括我，过去都说过不恰当的话。各位，先别急着举起干草叉和火把。毕竟“无罪者方可投石”嘛。
comments.text: I've been incredibly vocal about my stance on depression here on HN in the past, specifically that saying things like "man up" is absurd. Depression, like every other disease on the planet, is not something you "man up" through. It's a disease that happens to manifest itself in the same places that personality does. To a casual, uninformed observer, depression is a choice of behavior. It isn't. You don't get depression from weakness in the same way that you don't get cancer from weakness. Depression also kills more people per year than cancer does. Cancer about 20,000 -- depression about 30,000. (Highly relevant lecture by a very brilliant neuroscientist: [VIDEO] ) -- That said, Ed Weissman made an inappropriate comment. Every single person here, including me, has made inappropriate comments in the past. Let's not start the pitchforks and torches just yet, guys. He who is without sin, and all that.

comments.text_zh: 抑郁症与激素变化相关，但说它是激素变化的结果则是还原论式的，也不准确。抑郁症也与被称为 cytokines 的炎症标志物的变化高度相关[1]，但把它归结为单一生物因素，从来都不能得出准确的发病机制。Robert Sapolsky 的 Stanford 讲座很好地概述了导致抑郁症的主要风险因素之间的相互作用和关系[2]。[1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO] [Robert Sapolsky On Depression]
comments.text: Depression correlates with hormonal changes, but saying it's a result of it is reductionistic and inaccurate. Depression also highly correlates with changes in inflammatory markers called cytokines[1], but reducing it to a single biological factor never yields an accurate pathogenesis of the disease. Robert Sapolskys Stanford Lecture gives a good overview of the interaction an relationship of the main risk factors causing depression[2]. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO] [Robert Sapolsky On Depression]

comments.author: g3e0
comments.story_title: Surviving Depression
comments.text_zh: 看到抗抑郁药被描述成“快乐丸”、会“麻痹你的感官”，我觉得非常令人沮丧。这样的评论只会加深围绕这些药物的污名。这种污名正是我拖了好几年才去求助的部分原因。我服用 Mirtazapine 的体验恰恰相反。在我抑郁最深的时候，那才是我“麻木”的时候。和很多人一样，我抑郁时会听悲伤的音乐，但后来悲伤的音乐也不再让我感到悲伤了，我真的就只是什么都感觉不到。自从服用 Mirtazapine 以来，我13年来第一次摆脱了抑郁，它彻底改变了我的生活。我仍然拥有完整的人类情绪范围——我有心情好/心情差的时候（大部分时候好），有觉得无聊/一般般的日子，看电影的悲伤片段会哭。抗抑郁药治好了我的抑郁，它们并没有给我一种虚假的、膨胀的幸福感。“我真的快乐吗？”这个问题甚至都不太会出现在我脑海里。我只是感到满足。我经历的唯副作用是刚开始服药时极度疲惫了3天，之后就消退了。还有我的食欲增加了，所以胖了几磅，但因为我本来就很瘦，而且已经开始举铁，所以这算是净收益。我觉得斯坦福教授 Robert Sapolsky 的这个讲座非常有见地——[视频]——我们都会抑郁，这是生活的正常部分，但抑郁症是一种疾病，它会让你无缘无故地一直抑郁下去。
comments.text: I find it very disheartening to see antidepressants described as "happy pills" that "numb your senses". Comments like this only serve to reinforce the stigma around these medications. This stigma is the part of the reason why I held out from seeking help for years. My experience taking Mirtazapine has been the exact opposite. At the deepest point of my depression, that is when I was "numb". Like many people I would listen to sad music when I was depressed, but eventually sad music didn't make me feel sad anymore, I literally just felt nothing. Since being on Mirtazapine, my depression is gone for the first time in 13 years and it's completely changed my life. I still have the full human emotional range - I have good/bad moods (mostly good), days where I feel bored/meh, I cry at the sad parts in films. The antidepressants cured my depression, they haven't given me a false sense of inflated happiness. The question of "am I actually happy?" doesn't even really cross my mind. I'm just content. The only side effects I experienced were 3 days of extreme tiredness when I first started taking them, which then subsided. And my appetite increased, so I have gained a few pounds, but since I was already quite skinny and had started lifting weights, this has been a net plus. I found this lecture by Stanford professor Robert Sapolsky highly insightful - [VIDEO] - We all get depressed, it's a normal part of life, but depression is a disease which causes you to stay depressed for no reason,

comments.why_zh: 关于抑郁症中 learned helplessness 的资料来源。
comments.text_zh: > 对我来说，关键在于不要把自己说服到悲伤里去。完全正确。你学到的一个工具是想法/感受/行动如何相互作用：你无法控制自己的感受，但感受会影响你的想法。你可以控制自己的行动，而行动至少能影响一部分感受。你可以控制一部分想法，而想法会影响你的感受。（我可能没有完全准确地表述这一点，但大意是一样的。）所以基本上你会学到：如果你开始“投资”于更健康的行动和想法（也就是说，不要闷闷不乐、自怜或反刍），它会慢慢见效，让负面感受变少。不，它不能解决你生活里的每一个问题，但抑郁症的一大部分是“learned helplessness” [1]，而了解想法/感受/行动可以成为对抗它的第一个工具。[1]. [VIDEO]
comments.text: > for me it was about NOT talking oneself into sadness. Exactly. one tool you learn is how your thoughts/feelings/actions interact: You cannot control your feelings, but they do influence your thoughts. You can control your actions, but they can influence at least some of your feelings. You can control some of your thoughts, which will influence your feelings. (I may not have stated this exactly correctly, but the gist is the same ). So basically you learn that if you begin "investing" in healthier actions and thoughts (i.e. not sulking or self-pity or rumination), it will slowly pay off in less negative feelings. No it doesnt' solve every single problem in your life, but a big part of depression is "learned helplessness" [1], and learning about thoughts/feelings/actions can be the first tool to counter this. [1]. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 抑郁症并不是一个被很好理解的现象。在这样的讨论中，留意“抑郁”这个词的含义至关重要。它在口语中被当作“难过”“悲伤”或者只是“今天心情不好”的同义词。我说我抑郁了，是因为我妈妈去世了。这通常的意思是“因为某个非常亲近的人最近去世了，我正在经历自然的哀伤过程”。Robert Sapolsky 对这一点解释得比我好得多[1]。我带着重度抑郁生活了大约三十年。治疗过程令人沮丧。你会经历他们所用的各种诊断流程。然后他们就往你身上扔药片。这个也许有用，吃三周——三个月，然后告诉我们你感觉如何。你得吃足够长的时间，才能确保它“完全起效”。有些药会让你更抑郁、更想自杀。有些有其它严重的副作用。如果给你治疗的医生认为你试一种药已经够久了，他们就会往你身上扔另一种药，然后你再重复一遍，直到你感觉好些。接着他们开始尝试联合用药。那就更有意思了。我多年来大部分时间都在当小白鼠，病情越来越糟，还得应付各种副作用。我在这件事上并不特殊。重度抑郁常见的情况就是试药、失败、试药、失败、试药、失败。据我所知，我们没有物理手段来诊断抑郁症。你没法去急诊室让他们测点什么，然后告诉你有没有抑郁。我们不知道它的成因（我们有很多关于可能的成因的想法，但
comments.text: Depression is not a well understood phenomenon. It is vital in such a discussion to be mindful of the term "depression".
